kjv: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him
mine: Behold, he will kill me; I have no hope
note: the ketiv lo' 'ayahel "I will not wait/hope" and the qere lo 'ayahel "for him I will wait" differ in one letter; the KJV follows the qere and produces a famous confession of faith, while the ketiv (which fits "yet I will argue my ways to his face") makes it a statement of defiance in despair. Context: I have no hope (of surviving), yet I will argue my case (medium confidence). 13:14 'I will put my life in my hand' expects death; 13:15b 'yet I will argue my ways to his face' and 13:16-18 'I know I shall be vindicated' make defiance with hope of vindication, not trust in being spared.

kjv: Your remembrances [are] like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay
mine: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay
note: zikhronekhem are their memorable sayings, and gabbekhem their "bosses/defences" (shield bosses, breastworks), not bodies.
